title: test(lint): derive the list-view position-coverage criterion from the rule
body:
Fixes #18836

Clause-②: no

The test table's docblock claimed two directions and the assertion under it carried one. This replaces the floor with a criterion derived from the rule's own tables, and makes the docblock true.

## The premise, re-measured

Every reading below was taken on this branch's base, `origin/main` `36583e989b` — the dispatch quoted `a43b9d0654`, this worktree branched later, so the numbers were re-taken rather than inherited. They land in the same place:

- docblock: `packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.test.ts:205-210`, still word for word `a position added to the rule without a row here leaves the count assertion below short`
- the assertion it points at: `:315`, `expect(cases.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(51)`
- `cases.length` at that commit: **52**

Both directions were measured by mutating the rule's `POSITIONS` table on disk and running the rule's own test file. Each mutation proved itself on disk (anchor count 1 before, 0 after; injected line count 1; blob hash moved) and was restored under a trap, with `git diff HEAD` proving the restore byte for byte.

| direction | mutation | before this PR | after this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| one — a position **dropped** from the rule fails here | remove `tree.labelField` | 1 failed / 129 passed | **2 failed** / 129 passed (of 131) — the per-case assertion AND the new sibling assertion |
| two — a position **added** to the rule with no row here | add `tree.ablationProbeField` | **130 passed, 0 failed** | **1 failed**, `covers every position the rule walks`, diff names `- "tree.ablationProbeField"` |

Direction two reported nothing at all: `cases.length` counts the rows of the test table, which a position added to the rule never moves, so the floor stayed true. That is the direction #18565 came in through. After this PR the failing assertion is the completeness one, and its diff names the offender (`- "tree.ablationProbeField"`).

Direction one is unchanged and still carried by the per-case assertions, exactly as the docblock's first half says — the failing test both before and after is `views[0].list.tree.labelField reports at warning`.

**A third reading the card did not claim.** The floor did not reliably do even its own advertised job. Deleting one row from the table (`tree.labelField`) on the base tree left **129 passed, 0 failed** — 52 rows against a floor of 51 is exactly one row of slack. The same deletion after this PR is red, and the failing assertion is the completeness one.

## Step 1 — does the new export reach a published entry?

`@objectstack/lint` is not private, `files` is `dist` / `README.md` / `CHANGELOG.md`, and `exports` has `.` and `./runtime` — so `src/` does not ship but `dist/` does. Re-measured on this base and it holds. Two facts about the barrels: `src/index.ts` re-exports this module by NAME (there is no `export *` in either barrel, count 0), and `src/runtime.ts` does not reference the module at all.

Readings after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint build`, grepping `dist/`. Bright control throughout: `validateListViewFieldRefs`, a symbol known to ship.

**Shape measured first — `export const X = Object.freeze([...])`:**

| `dist/` file | new symbol | bright control |
|---|---|---|
| `index.js` | 1 | 3 |
| `index.cjs` | 1 | 4 |
| `runtime.js` | 1 | 2 |
| `runtime.cjs` | 1 | 2 |
| `index.d.ts` | 0 | 2 |
| `index.d.cts` | 0 | 2 |
| `runtime.d.ts` / `runtime.d.cts` | 0 | 0 |
| `runtime-DAPAkqcs.d.ts` / `.d.cts` | 0 | not present |

A raw count in a bundle body is not a published entry, so the export layer was measured separately. In `dist/index.js`'s `export {}` clause: new symbol 0, against 1 each for `validateListViewFieldRefs`, `LIST_VIEW_FIELD_DOTTED` and `LIST_VIEW_FIELD_UNKNOWN`. In `dist/index.cjs`'s `__export` map: new symbol 0, controls 1 each. Dark control for that layer: `COLUMN_ENTRY_POSITIONS`, a module const the rule has never exported, reads **2** in `index.js` and 2 in `index.cjs` — a name in the bundle body is genuinely no evidence of a published entry.

Under this shape four `dist` JS files moved bytes (esbuild keeps a frozen initializer as dead weight); all four `.d.ts` / `.d.cts` files were byte-identical.

**Shape shipped — `export function listViewWalkedPositions()`:** the symbol is tree-shaken. 0 occurrences in all eight published files, while the bright control still reads 3 / 4 / 2 with the same instrument on the same files.

> ⚠️ **Corrected by the dispatching seat after the contract review, ⛔ not by the author.** This paragraph first read 「all nine `dist/` artifacts byte-identical … 9 of 9 OK」. The measured face is **14 artifacts, of which 10 are byte-identical** — the 4 JS bundles and all 6 type files — and **4 source maps moved** (`index.js.map`, `index.cjs.map`, `runtime.js.map`, `runtime.cjs.map`; `files[]` ships `dist` whole, so they are published). Their differing keys are `mappings` and `names` only, `sources` are equal, and the new symbol is absent from `names` in all four ⇒ a line offset, ⛔ not a surface. The original count hashed 9 files and omitted the 4 maps and one `runtime-*.d.cts`. Measured twice independently: by the at-tier contract review (record `5724912914`) and again by the author in its rework report. The reading the paragraph rests on is unchanged; only the count was wrong.

**Reading: the new export reaches no published entry and moves zero bytes of the published artifact.** Per the dispatch's step-2 table, that is route A, and route A is what this PR implements.

### On the declaration line above

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` was the dispatch's mechanical floor, declared before this measurement existed and routed for the seat's contract review. The at-tier review (record `5724912914`) **overturned it to `no`**, with no direction arm — the diff widens no accept set and expands no public surface. Per `references/lanes/spec.md:20` a conservative `yes` is never an error, so the overturn is by design and is ⛔ not a fault of the author.

> ⚠️ **Rewritten by the dispatching seat, ⛔ not by the author** — the charter gives the author exactly one body write and routes later corrections through the seat. The changeset that graded this `minor` has been **deleted** by the author in the rework, and the PR carries `skip-changeset` instead: measured, the `fixed` group of about 70 packages would otherwise all move to 17.5.0 for a change that delivers **0 changed code or type bytes** to any consumer.

## What changed

**`validate-list-view-field-refs.ts`** gains one module-level export, `listViewWalkedPositions()`, which derives the `block.key` id of every field-naming position from the rule's own `POSITIONS` and `COLUMN_ENTRY_POSITIONS` tables. 52 positions today. No `POSITIONS` row is touched — not a position, not a tier, not a severity — and the barrel is untouched.

**`validate-list-view-field-refs.test.ts`**: the floor becomes set equality between the positions the rule walks and the positions this file's two case tables assert. The five-row measured table moves to module scope because three positions (`grouping.fields`, `kanban.groupByField`, `gantt.startDateField`) are asserted there and nowhere else; a criterion reading only the sibling table would need a hand-written exemption for them, which is the kind of constant this card is about. The per-case assertion bodies are unchanged, byte for byte.

## Why set equality and not the count equality route A suggested

Route A said: derive the count from `POSITIONS` and compare it to `cases.length`. That equality cannot be written without magic constants, because rows are not positions:

- 52 rows in the second table and 52 positions walked — the same number over different sets, by coincidence.
- 3 positions are asserted only in the sibling five-row table.
- 2 rows in the second table (and 1 in the first) assert the rule's hard-coded filter walks, which no table declares.
- 2 positions carry two rows each (`columns` and `gantt.tooltipFields`: once as a bare name, once as a record with a `field` key), so the second table holds 1 duplicate row.

The arithmetic a count equality would have had to hard-code is `52 = 52 - 3 + 2 + 1`. Set equality states the property directly instead, names the offending position in the failure diff, and needs no constant at all. Per the dispatch's own zoning this is the suggested-route zone, so it is reported rather than silently taken: the ruling (measurement decides A vs B) is executed as written.

**What the new assertion does NOT carry**, stated in the code so it cannot become the next overclaim: it is one-directional. `positionAsserted` answers only with positions the rule currently walks, so a row for a position the rule has dropped contributes to neither side and the assertion stays green — that direction belongs to the per-case assertions, and both halves are measured above. A first draft of the comment claimed both directions; the direction-one probe showed only the per-case assertion firing, and the comment was corrected before the first push rather than shipped.

## docblock, sentence by sentence

| original | now | true? | held by what |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Every remaining position, with the severity tier it earns.` | unchanged | yes | the per-case rows, each asserting one path and one severity |
| `The table is the readable half of the rule's own POSITIONS table` | unchanged | yes, and now mechanically so | the completeness assertion reads the rule's tables directly |
| `a position dropped from the rule fails here` | unchanged | yes | the per-case assertions — measured red before and after |
| `a position added to the rule without a row here leaves the count assertion below short` | `a position added to the rule without a row in either table fails the completeness assertion below — which derives the set of positions from the rule's own tables instead of counting this one's rows` | yes | the new set-equality assertion — measured green before, red after |

## The inline comment above the assertion

The dispatch fenced it as accurate and not to be rewritten as if it were the defect. It is not rewritten as a finding — it is replaced because the assertion it annotates no longer exists, and the dispatch also forbids leaving a floor and an equality side by side. Its semantics were right; the one-row slack measured above is reported as a reading, not fixed as a second thing.

## Verification

Run through the shared verify lock. Package: `@objectstack/lint`.

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` | 104 files / 3909 tests passed | 104 files / **3910** tests passed (the delta is the one new `it`) |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` | — | exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`: 2 files / 6 errors / 2 pinned signatures held) |
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide, `eslint . --no-inline-config`) | — | exit 0 |
| control-character self-scan over the three touched files | — | no match |

Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **51** families from this tree at `9897eaae29` (58 at the previous head; the 7 that left are the changeset families, since the changeset was deleted); all 51 were run and each exit code recorded before any pipe, then reconciled with `--ran`. **48 green, 3 NOT MEASURED** — `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:type-check-debt` each exited 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: all three read built output across the whole repo, which this worktree does not have. They are neither a pass nor a failure here, and CI builds fresh and runs them. The `dist` byte-identity measured above is why this diff cannot move their verdict.

Dependency-closure build: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build`, exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- Nothing outside this card's scope was changed. The `POSITIONS` table, the package barrel and the per-case assertion bodies are untouched; the only positions-table edits in this branch were the two ablation mutations, each restored and proven restored.
- Noted, not filed: the replaced floor had exactly one row of slack (52 rows against 51), so a single silent row deletion passed it. It is fixed here as a consequence of replacing the assertion, so there is no separate card; the reading is above. Carrier: this PR.
- Noted, not filed: `dist/runtime.js` bundles `validateListViewFieldRefs` although `dist/runtime.d.ts` exports it nowhere. That is the documented consequence of `splitting: false` in `packages/lint/tsup.config.ts`, whose own header carries the measurement, not a defect. Carrier: none.



> ⚠️ **Five cells refreshed by the dispatching seat at the reworked head, ⛔ not by the author.** They described head `270d9f4b35`; this PR is now at `9897eaae29`. Refreshed: the direction-one "after" cell (the rework made that direction fail TWICE — the per-case assertion and the new sibling assertion — where it previously failed once), the direction-two "after" cell (now quoted by the failing assertion's own name and diff), the one-row-slack sentence (its post-PR count moved with the new `it`), the test count (3909 → 3910) and the gates paragraph (58 → 51 families, because deleting the changeset removed 7 changeset families). ⭐ The direction-one and direction-two readings were **re-verified by the at-tier review at this head** (record `5725290629`); the gates and test counts are the **author's** readings at this head, taken from its rework report and ⛔ not re-run by the seat. ⛔ No reading here was weakened: every refresh describes the same or stronger protection.
